title: Prefixes, suffixes & roots
examples: How do I figure out what this long word means?
Can you give me more examples of Latin roots?
Does knowing the root help me with spelling?

explain.say: Today we are learning about word parts. These parts help us understand new words.
A root is the main part of a word. It carries the main meaning of the word.

draw.text: Root: Core meaning of a word

explain.say: A prefix goes at the beginning of a root. It changes the word's meaning slightly.
A suffix goes at the end of a root. It often changes the word's job in a sentence.
For example, the root 'port' means to carry. 'Export' means to carry out.
In real life, when you read a label, roots help you know what it does. A 'hydro' root means water.

faq.q: How do I know if a word part is a prefix or a suffix?
faq.a: Prefixes always go at the beginning of the root word. Suffixes always attach to the end of the root word.
asks: Where does the added part go?
Is it always at the start or always at the end?

faq.q: Can I use these parts to guess the meaning of a brand new word?
faq.a: Yes, knowing the common roots helps you guess the general meaning. You can look up the root word first.
asks: Does this help with spelling too?

faq.q: Are all roots from Greek or Latin?
faq.a: Many common roots come from Greek or Latin. However, some roots come from Old English too.
asks: Do I only learn Greek roots?
Are there other sources for roots?

faq.q: If I change the root, does the whole word change meaning?
faq.a: Yes, changing the root changes the core meaning. For example, 'read' is different from 'write'.
asks: Does the root carry the main idea?
If I change the middle part, what happens?

faq.q: What is the difference between a root and a prefix?
faq.a: The root is the core word meaning. The prefix is a small addition that changes the meaning at the start.
asks: Which part is the most important?
Can a word have both a root and a prefix?

facts: Roots are the core part of a word that holds the main meaning.
Prefixes are added to the beginning of a root to change its meaning.
Suffixes are added to the end of a root, sometimes changing the word's type.
Many common roots come from ancient languages like Latin and Greek.

quiz.say: What is the root word in 'unbelievable'?
quiz.why: The root 'believe' carries the core meaning of faith or trust.

wrong.1: This is the prefix, which only changes the meaning, not the core idea.
wrong.2: This is a suffix, which changes the word's grammatical job.
wrong.3: This is not a real word part combination.

quiz.say: If 'aqua' means water, what does 'aquarium' likely mean?

options.show: A place or container for water
options.say: A place or container for water

quiz.why: The root 'aqua' tells you the topic is water, and '-arium' suggests a place.

wrong.0: This is too vague and doesn't use word structure knowledge.
wrong.2: This confuses the meaning of the suffix '-arium'.
wrong.3: This ignores the meaning of the suffix entirely.

quiz.say: Which word is formed by adding a prefix to the root 'view'?
quiz.why: Adding the prefix 're-' at the start means to do something again.

wrong.1: This adds a suffix, changing the word to a person.
wrong.2: This adds a suffix, changing the word to an action.
wrong.3: This incorrectly places the prefix after the root.
